title: Statistics and experimental design for brain and behavioral science
stage: College neuroscience and cognitive science degree
audience: a college student in a neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology or biology degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn to design experiments on brains and behavior and to analyze their data honestly, in Python: describing data, sampling distributions and confidence intervals, t-tests and their assumptions, effect sizes and power, analysis of variance and factorial designs, correlation and regression, repeated measures and mixed-effects models in outline, nonparametric and permutation tests, the bootstrap, multiple comparisons, and preregistration and the habits that prevent false findings.

weeks.1: Describing data and the logic of experiments
weeks.3: T-tests: one sample, paired and independent
weeks.5: Analysis of variance and factorial designs
weeks.8: Repeated measures and mixed-effects models in outline
weeks.9: Nonparametric tests, permutation tests and the bootstrap
weeks.10: Multiple comparisons: Bonferroni and false discovery rate
weeks.11: Preregistration, questionable research practices and replication
weeks.12: Reporting results: figures in words, tables and honest claims

blocks.deliverable: Compute and interpret confidence intervals in code.
Choose a sample size for a planned experiment.
Week 7 midterm; analyze a within-subject experiment correctly.
Run a permutation test and correct a family of tests.
Write a preregistration for a small experiment.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Analysis report: analyze a supplied data set from a reaction-time experiment with two factors, in plain Python written without statistics libraries for the core tests, from cleaning to effect sizes, intervals, a permutation check and a correction for multiple tests, and write a short results section that a reviewer would accept.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
